title: Resolve the published ligature loss and require specificity on conditional controls
statement: The printed Rule 6 in Matlach, Janečková and Dostál has a loss of at least 1 for distinct candidates, since the largest symbol probability and the smaller candidate probability sum to at most 1. Table 5 reports smaller Rule 6 values, including 0.299, with Rule 6 weight 1. In Rule 3 the equation sums probability in shared contexts and the prose describes the mass in unmatched contexts. I retained all eight weights and compared the literal equations with one plausible reconstruction of Rules 3 and 6. In both calculations five of six fully planted triplets that remained in the eligible alphabet ranked below the fifth percentile across matched English, Latin and Italian controls. Three other plants could not enter the candidate universe because the replacement or a component fell below frequency support. In unmodified natural controls 9–12 candidate symbols acquired a fifth-percentile triplet even though no ligatures were inserted. In six stationary whole-copy line-chain controls 10–13 of 17 symbols did so. More specifically, m with components i,d and q with i,e rank below the fifth percentile in both public ZL and Takahashi and in all six line-chain controls under both reconstructions. Those control glyphs are emitted directly without the tested pair-to-glyph substitutions. Three separate Yale scan checks also confirm real differences across the pinned transcriptions at disputed raw pair occurrences. The published percentile measures the rank among scored candidates and can be low for an explicitly unfused symbol.
check: Recover the authors' original executable specification or reconcile Table 5 with the equations before claiming numerical reproduction. Calibrate a fixed candidate-level error criterion against text controls matched for rare transitions and word position, with independently planted ligatures across several rates and replacement probabilities. Test shared triplets in separate ZL and Takahashi blocks and adjudicate disputed appearances on scans with glyph candidates masked.

source.where: Detecting the ligatures, Rules 3 and 6, Table 5 and S2 Fig

practice.score: Use the printed weighted sum and exactly 1,100,1,1,100,1,1,10 as the eight weights. Estimate joint adjacent symbol frequencies with single spaces and zero a transition whose share of the originating row or receiving column is less than 0.002. For literal Rule 3, sum rarer-sign left-context mass where the commoner sign is observed. For the reconstruction sum the complementary mass, and replace Rule 6 (1−minimum candidate probability)/maximum symbol probability by 1−(minimum candidate probability/maximum symbol probability). The alternative is an explicit reconstruction. For Rule 4 with fewer than two realized contexts set loss zero, and treat other undefined Pearson coefficients as zero correlation. Score all ordered triples with C distinct from either component. Retain the same-symbol penalty when A equals B.
practice.eligibility: Candidate universe uses non-space symbols with relative incidence greater than 500/229431, matching the published absolute threshold after scaling to this sample length. Space remains in the transition matrix. For the special n → i plus space test and below-threshold signs, calculate their percentile against the same universe and mark them as noncompeting. Count ranks at or below the candidate score, including ties. An outsider below every competing score receives empirical percentile zero.
practice.data: Manuscript comparison uses shared certain paragraph-line IDs from official public practice ZL and Takahashi with all certain words as transcribed. Each pinned natural control is a cleaned lowercase ASCII prefix of 31,350 symbols including spaces. For each preselected pair, replace every nonoverlapping occurrence by a new atomic symbol X in a separate copy of the control. At most one such substitution process is planted per sample. The copying controls use the P-R-009 stationary line chain fit on public practice-training ZL, seeds 421–426, over the public practice layout. The line chain emits EVA-basic units directly. The reported fixed manuscript candidates occur as separate emitted EVA units where relevant to the cited false positives.

scan_checks.statement: The two final signs on the right reproduce S2 A’s first detail. The last has a small upper loop and a thin descending stroke. ZL has final sg, while Takahashi and Friedman have sm. The scan provides the locus and graphic shape without fixing a universal transcription rule.

The line-final bench word at the edge of the painted area reproduces S2 A’s second detail. The final shape is looped with a hooked tail. ZL joins sg, Takahashi joins sm, and Friedman separates the final g.

The disputed third token corresponds to S2 E. The final figure-eight is clear. Two low strokes before it are hard to classify by this crop. Takahashi gives oriid and both ZL and Friedman give oreed. This split affects naked id counts.
